title: A Sponge Under the Sea
ru: Кто такой Губка Боб, где он живёт и кто его друзья
text:
SpongeBob SquarePants is a cartoon from the USA. It starts in 1999. The creator is Stephen Hillenburg. He loves the sea and sea animals.

SpongeBob is a yellow sponge. He is kind and very happy. He lives in a pineapple under the sea. His town is Bikini Bottom.

SpongeBob has a job. He makes burgers at the Krusty Krab. His boss is Mr. Krabs. Mr. Krabs is a crab, and he loves money.

His best friend is Patrick. Patrick is a pink starfish. He is funny, but not very smart. Squidward is their neighbor. He does not like noise.

The show is silly and colorful. Children love it, and many adults love it too.

questions.q: Where does SpongeBob live?
What does SpongeBob make at work?
Who is Patrick?

title: Peppa and Her Family
ru: Простой рассказ о свинке Пеппе и её семье
text:
Peppa Pig is a cartoon from the UK. It starts in 2004. It is for very small children.

Peppa is a little pink pig. She lives in a house on a hill. She lives with her mom, her dad and her little brother George. George loves his toy dinosaur.

Peppa has many friends. They are animals too. Her best friend is Suzy Sheep.

Peppa likes games and music. She loves muddy puddles. She jumps in them with her boots on. Her family often jumps with her!

The episodes are very short. The pictures are simple and bright. The English is slow and clear. So many adults watch Peppa Pig to learn English. It is a good idea!

questions.q: What is the name of Peppa's brother?
What does George love?
Why do some adults watch Peppa Pig?

title: A Cat and a Mouse
ru: Вечная погоня кота и мыши без слов
text:
Tom and Jerry is a very old cartoon. It starts in 1940 in the USA. The creators are William Hanna and Joseph Barbera.

Tom is a gray and white cat. Jerry is a small brown mouse. Tom wants to catch Jerry. But Jerry is fast and very smart. Tom never wins.

The two animals run all over the house. They break plates and chairs. They play tricks on each other. It is crazy and very funny.

The characters almost never talk. We only hear music and noise. So you do not need any language for this cartoon. People in every country can watch it.

Tom and Jerry are enemies. But sometimes they are friends too!

questions.q: Who is Jerry?
Does Tom often catch Jerry?
Why can people in every country watch it?

title: A Green Ogre
ru: Знакомство с огром Шреком и его друзьями
text:
Shrek is a cartoon film from 2001. It comes from the studio DreamWorks in the USA.

Shrek is a big green ogre. He lives alone in a swamp. He is not very friendly. He likes his quiet home and his mud.

One day many fairy tale characters come to his swamp. Shrek is angry. He wants his home back. So he goes on a trip.

On the trip he meets Donkey. Donkey talks all the time. He is loud, but he is a good friend. Later they meet Princess Fiona. She is brave and strong.

The film is a funny fairy tale. The hero is not a prince. He is an ogre! Adults and children love it.

questions.q: Where does Shrek live?
What is Donkey like?
What color is Shrek?

title: Toys Are Alive
ru: Первый полностью компьютерный мультфильм: живые игрушки
text:
Toy Story is a film from 1995. It comes from the studio Pixar. It is special. It is the first long film made fully on computers.

The film is about toys. When people are in the room, the toys do not move. When people go away, the toys are alive! They walk, talk and play.

The toys belong to a boy, Andy. Woody is a cowboy toy. He is Andy's favorite. Then Andy gets a new toy, Buzz Lightyear. Buzz is a space ranger. He thinks he is a real hero from space.

Woody is not happy. He is jealous of Buzz. But later they are best friends.

The film is funny and warm. It has four more parts.

questions.q: Who is Woody?
What do the toys do when people go away?
Why is Toy Story special?
o: It is the first long film made fully on computers

title: A Little Fish
ru: Папа-рыбка ищет сына в огромном океане
text:
Finding Nemo is a film from 2003. It comes from Pixar. The story is under the sea.

Nemo is a little orange and white fish. He is a clownfish. He lives with his dad, Marlin. Marlin loves his son very much. But he is always afraid.

One day a diver takes Nemo. Now Nemo is far from home. Marlin swims across the big ocean to find him.

He is not alone. He meets Dory, a blue fish. Dory is very kind and happy. But she has a problem. She forgets things very fast! She is often funny.

The sea in the film is beautiful. There are turtles, sharks and many colors. It is a great film about family.

questions.q: Who is Marlin?
What is Dory's problem?
What kind of fish is Nemo?

title: Two Sisters and Snow
ru: Две сестры, снежная магия и весёлый снеговик
text:
Frozen is a Disney film from 2013. It is a story about two sisters. Their names are Elsa and Anna. They live in a kingdom, Arendelle.

Elsa is the older sister. She has magic. She can make ice and snow with her hands. But she cannot control her magic well. She is often afraid.

Anna is the younger sister. She is brave, funny and very open. She loves her sister very much.

There is a funny snowman in the film too. His name is Olaf. He loves summer and warm hugs!

The film has a lot of songs. Many children know them. The main idea is simple: family and love are very important.

questions.q: What can Elsa do?
Who is Olaf?
Who is the older sister?

title: Small, Yellow and Funny
ru: Кто такие миньоны и почему их все любят
text:
Minions are small yellow characters. They are from the film Despicable Me (2010). The studio is Illumination. Later, in 2015, the Minions get their own film.

Minions look like little capsules. They wear blue jeans and big glasses. Some Minions have one eye, and some have two eyes.

They work for a bad boss. In Despicable Me, their boss is Gru. But the Minions are not really bad. They are just silly and funny.

Minions have their own language. It is a funny mix of many languages. People do not understand all the words, but they laugh.

And Minions love one food very much. It is bananas!

questions.q: What color are Minions?
What food do Minions love?
Who is their boss in Despicable Me?

title: The Young Lion
ru: История львёнка Симбы в Африке (без спойлеров)
text:
The Lion King is a Disney film from 1994. The story is in Africa. All the characters are animals.

Simba is a young lion. His father is Mufasa. Mufasa is the king. He is big, strong and wise. Simba wants to be king one day too.

Simba has an uncle, Scar. Scar is not a good lion. He wants to be king. He has a bad plan. (No big spoilers here!)

Later Simba meets two new friends. Timon is a small meerkat. Pumbaa is a warthog. They are very funny. They have an easy life with no problems.

The film has great music and beautiful pictures of Africa. Many people call it the best Disney film.

questions.q: Who is Mufasa?
Where is the story?
What animal is Timon?

title: A Panda Who Loves Kung Fu
ru: Толстый панда По мечтает стать мастером кунг-фу
text:
Kung Fu Panda is a film from 2008. It comes from DreamWorks. The story is in old China.

Po is a big panda. He works in a noodle shop. His dad is a goose, Mr. Ping. Yes, a goose! Po loves food very much. He eats a lot.

Po has a big dream. He wants to do kung fu. He knows all about the Furious Five. They are five great kung fu masters. But Po is fat and slow. He cannot fight well.

Then something big happens. Now Po must learn kung fu. His teacher is Master Shifu. Shifu is small, but very strict.

The film is funny and kind. Jack Black is the voice of Po.

questions.q: Where does Po work?
What animal is Po's dad?
Who is Po's teacher?

title: A World of Cars
ru: Гоночная машина Молния Маккуин в маленьком городке
text:
Cars is a Pixar film from 2006. In this film there are no people. All the characters are cars! They talk, eat and live in towns.

Lightning McQueen is a red race car. He is young and very fast. He wants to win a big race. But he is not a nice car. He thinks only about himself.

One day he gets lost. He is in a small, old town, Radiator Springs. The town is quiet and a little sad. Lightning does not like it.

But he meets new friends there. His best friend is Mater. Mater is an old tow truck. He is funny and very kind.

The film is about friendship. Speed is not everything!

questions.q: What color is Lightning McQueen?
Who is Mater?
What is the film about?

title: A Bear Who Loves Honey
ru: Медвежонок Пух и его друзья из Чудесного леса
text:
Winnie the Pooh is a little yellow bear. He comes from books by the English writer A. A. Milne. The first book is from 1926. Later Disney makes cartoons about him.

Pooh lives in a forest, the Hundred Acre Wood. He is kind and a little slow. His favorite food is honey. He always wants more honey!

Pooh has many friends. Piglet is small and often afraid. Eeyore is a gray donkey. He is always sad. Tigger is a tiger. He loves to jump. Christopher Robin is a boy. He is everyone's friend.

The stories are quiet and warm. Nothing bad happens. That is why adults read them to children at night.

questions.q: What is Pooh's favorite food?
Who is always sad?
Who writes the books about Pooh?

title: Six Friends in New York
ru: Шесть друзей, Нью-Йорк и любимое кафе — знаменитый ситком «Друзья».
text:
Friends is an American TV show. It is a comedy. The show starts in 1994 and ends in 2004. It has ten seasons.

The show is about six friends. Their names are Rachel, Monica, Phoebe, Joey, Chandler and Ross. They live in New York. They are young and they are not rich.

The friends often sit in a small café. They drink coffee and talk. They talk about work, love and family. They have funny problems every day.

Monica loves cooking. Joey wants to be an actor. Phoebe plays the guitar and sings strange songs.

Many people watch Friends today. It is easy and kind. It is a good show for English learners.

questions.q: Where do the friends live?
How many friends are in the show?
What does Joey want to be?

title: A Yellow Family
ru: Жёлтая семья из Спрингфилда: кто есть кто в «Симпсонах».
text:
The Simpsons is an American cartoon. Matt Groening makes it. The first episode is from 1989. The show is very old, but it is still on TV.

The Simpsons are a family. They live in a town called Springfield. Homer is the dad. He is fat and lazy, and he loves donuts. He works at a power plant. Marge is the mom. She has very tall blue hair.

They have three children. Bart is ten. He is naughty and funny. Lisa is eight. She is very clever and plays the saxophone. Maggie is a baby.

All the people in the show have yellow skin. The show is funny for kids and for adults.

questions.q: What color is Marge's hair?
What does Lisa play?
Where does Homer work?

title: A Man With No Words
ru: Мистер Бин почти не говорит, но его понимают во всём мире.
text:
Mr. Bean is a British comedy show. It starts in 1990. The actor is Rowan Atkinson.

Mr. Bean is a strange man. He wears a brown jacket and a thin red tie. He lives alone in a small flat. His best friend is a teddy bear. He has a small green car.

Mr. Bean does not talk much. He only makes funny faces and sounds. He does simple things, like shopping or cooking. But everything goes wrong!

This is why people all over the world love Mr. Bean. You do not need English to watch it. You only need your eyes. Children and adults laugh at him.

questions.q: Who is Mr. Bean's best friend?
What color is his car?
Why can everyone watch Mr. Bean?

title: A Blue Box in Time
ru: Доктор Кто — пришелец, который путешествует во времени в синей будке.
text:
Doctor Who is a British TV show. It is on the BBC. The first episode is from 1963. It is one of the oldest shows in the world.

The main hero is the Doctor. The Doctor is not a human. The Doctor is an alien from another planet. The Doctor is very old and very clever.

The Doctor has a time machine. It is called the TARDIS. It looks like a small blue box. But inside it is very, very big!

The Doctor travels in time and space. The Doctor visits the past, the future and other planets. The Doctor can change face and body. So many different actors can play the role.

questions.q: What does the TARDIS look like?
Is the Doctor a human?
Why can many actors play the Doctor?

title: Kids, Bikes and Mystery
ru: Дети на велосипедах, 80-е и тайна маленького городка — «Очень странные дела».
text:
Stranger Things is an American show on Netflix. It starts in 2016. The creators are two brothers, Matt and Ross Duffer.

The story is in the 1980s. It is in a small American town called Hawkins. A group of friends live there. They ride bikes and play board games. They love their town, but something is wrong in it.

A strange girl comes to the town. Her name is Eleven. She has no hair and she can move things with her mind. She becomes their friend.

There is also a dark, scary world near Hawkins. The kids want to stop the danger. The show is scary, but it is also about friendship. No big spoilers here!

What can Eleven do?
What do the friends ride?

title: A Girl in Black
ru: Уэнсдэй Аддамс в необычной школе — мрачная и смешная история.
text:
Wednesday is an American show on Netflix. It starts in 2022. Tim Burton directs some episodes. Jenna Ortega plays the main role.

Wednesday Addams is a teenage girl. She is from the strange Addams family. She always wears black and white clothes. She has two long black braids. She does not smile, and she does not like people much.

Wednesday goes to a new school. It is called Nevermore Academy. The students there are not normal. Some are vampires, and some are werewolves.

Wednesday has a friend called Thing. Thing is just a hand, but it can walk and help her! The show is dark, but it is also very funny.

questions.q: What colors does Wednesday wear?
What is the name of her school?
What is Thing?

title: A World of Blocks
ru: Мир из кубиков, где можно построить всё что угодно.
text:
Minecraft is a video game. It is from Sweden. Markus Persson makes the first version. The full game comes out in 2011.

In Minecraft, the world is made of blocks. There are blocks of earth, stone, wood and water. You can break blocks and you can put them in new places.

You can play in two main ways. In one mode, you build. You can build a house, a castle or a big city. In the other mode, you survive. You need food and a safe home. At night, monsters come out! A green monster called a Creeper can destroy your house.

People of all ages play Minecraft. It is simple, but you can do almost anything.

questions.q: What is the Minecraft world made of?
When do monsters come out?
What color is a Creeper?

title: The Man in the Red Hat
ru: Марио — самый известный герой видеоигр из Японии.
text:
Mario is a very famous video game hero. He is from Japan. The company Nintendo makes the games. Shigeru Miyamoto creates Mario. The game Super Mario Bros. comes out in 1985.

Mario is a short man with a big moustache. He wears a red hat and blue overalls. He is a plumber. His brother is Luigi. Luigi is tall and wears green.

In the games, Mario runs and jumps a lot. He collects gold coins. A mushroom makes him big. His enemy is Bowser, a big bad turtle. Bowser often takes Princess Peach, and Mario must help her.

The games are colorful and happy. Many people play them with their families.

questions.q: What is Mario's job?
Who is Luigi?
What makes Mario big?

title: A Game From Moscow
ru: Тетрис придумал Алексей Пажитнов в Москве — и в него играет весь мир.
text:
Tetris is a very old and very famous game. It is from Russia! Alexey Pajitnov creates it in Moscow in 1984. He works with computers, and he loves puzzles.

The game is very simple. Shapes fall from the top of the screen. Every shape has four small squares. There are seven different shapes. You can move them left and right. You can also turn them.

You need to make full lines. When a line is full, it goes away. Then you get points. The game gets faster and faster. When the shapes reach the top, the game is over.

People play Tetris on computers, phones and game consoles. It is easy to learn, but it is hard to stop!

questions.q: Where is Tetris from?
What happens to a full line?
How many squares are in every shape?

title: Monsters in Your Pocket
ru: Покемоны — «карманные монстры» из Японии и жёлтый Пикачу.
text:
Pokémon is a big game series from Japan. The first games come out in 1996. Satoshi Tajiri is the creator. The name means "pocket monsters".

Pokémon are small creatures. There are many hundreds of them. Some are cute, and some are scary. They live in forests, in water and in caves. Every Pokémon has a special power, like fire, water or electricity.

In the games, you are a trainer. You find Pokémon and catch them in a small ball. Then you train them. Your Pokémon fight other Pokémon in friendly battles.

The most famous Pokémon is Pikachu. It is yellow and it has red cheeks. There are also cartoons, cards and toys.

questions.q: What does "Pokémon" mean?
What color is Pikachu?
Who are you in the games?

title: Make Your Own Life
ru: The Sims — игра, где ты строишь дом и управляешь жизнью человечков.
text:
The Sims is a computer game from the USA. It comes out in 2000. Will Wright creates it.

In the game, you make little people. They are called Sims. You choose their face, hair and clothes. Then you build a house for them. You choose every room, every chair and every lamp.

Sims live a normal life. They eat, sleep, work and take a shower. They make friends and fall in love. But they need your help. If you forget about them, they are hungry and sad!

Sims do not speak English. They speak a funny language with no real words. Above every Sim, there is a green diamond. Many people play The Sims for hours.

questions.q: What are the little people called?
What do you build for them?
What is above every Sim?

title: Who Is the Impostor?
ru: Among Us — игра про космический корабль и одного предателя в команде.
text:
Among Us is an online game. A small American studio, InnerSloth, makes it. It comes out in 2018. In 2020, it is suddenly very popular.

Up to ten players play together. They are small, colorful astronauts. They are on a spaceship. Most players are the crew. They do simple jobs, like fixing wires.

But one or two players are impostors. They are secret enemies. They try to stop the crew and break the ship.

When there is a problem, the players have a meeting. They talk and vote. Who is the impostor? Friends often lie to each other. It is very funny!

The game is cheap and simple. It is great to play with friends.

questions.q: Where are the players?
What do the players do in a meeting?
When is the game suddenly very popular?

title: A House That Flies
ru: Мультфильм Pixar о старике, который улетел в Южную Америку на доме с шариками.
text:
Up is an animated film from Pixar. It came out in 2009, and Pete Docter was one of the directors.

The main character is Carl Fredricksen. He is an old man, and he lives alone in a small house. When he was young, he and his wife Ellie had a big dream. They wanted to travel to a wild place in South America. But life was busy, and they never went there.

One day Carl decides to do something crazy. He ties thousands of balloons to his house, and the house flies into the sky! But Carl is not alone. A young boy called Russell is on the porch, and now he is part of the trip too.

In South America they meet a funny talking dog, Dug, and a big colourful bird. The adventure is exciting, but the film is also about love, loss and friendship.

Many people say the first ten minutes are the saddest part of any Pixar film. Get some tissues before you watch it!

questions.q: How does Carl make his house fly?
Who is on the porch when the house flies?
Where did Carl and Ellie want to travel?

title: Music, Family and Marigolds
ru: Мультфильм о мексиканском мальчике, который мечтает о музыке и попадает в Страну мёртвых.
text:
Coco is a Pixar film from 2017. The story happens in Mexico during the Day of the Dead. On this holiday, families remember relatives who died. They put photos, food and orange marigold flowers on special tables.

The hero is Miguel, a twelve-year-old boy. He loves music more than anything, and he wants to be a famous guitar player. But there is a big problem: his family hates music. Many years ago, a musician left the family, and after that music was not allowed in their home.

On the Day of the Dead, something magical happens. Miguel enters the Land of the Dead. It is a bright, colourful city full of skeletons. There he meets his dead relatives and a funny, clever man called Héctor. Miguel must get home before sunrise, or he will stay there forever.

Coco is beautiful to look at, and the music is great. It is also a warm story about family and memory. Many viewers say it made them cry, but in a good way.

questions.q: Where does the story happen?
Why is music a problem for Miguel?
When must Miguel get home?

title: A Rabbit in the Police
ru: Мультфильм Disney о крольчихе-полицейской и хитром лисе в городе животных.
text:
Zootopia is a Disney film from 2016. In some countries it has a different name, for example Zootropolis. It shows a big modern city where only animals live. Lions, elephants, mice and giraffes all work, shop and ride trains together.

The main character is Judy Hopps, a small rabbit from a farm. Her big dream is to be a police officer. Everyone says that rabbits are too small and too soft for this job. But Judy works harder than all the other students, and she becomes the first rabbit officer in the city.

At first, her boss gives her a boring job. Then some animals disappear, and Judy wants to find them. She needs help, so she works with Nick Wilde, a clever fox who tricks people for money. A rabbit and a fox are not natural friends, but they become a great team.

The film is funny, and the city looks amazing. It also has a serious idea: we should not judge others because of what they are.

questions.q: What is Judy's dream?
What animal is Nick Wilde?
What is the serious idea of the film?
o: Don't judge others by what they are

title: The Voices in Your Head
ru: Мультфильм Pixar об эмоциях, которые живут в голове девочки Райли.
text:
Inside Out is a Pixar film from 2015. Pete Docter directed it. The idea is very original: most of the story happens inside the head of a girl called Riley.

Riley is eleven years old. Her family moves from Minnesota to San Francisco, and she has a new house, a new school and no friends. This is a hard time for her.

In Riley's mind, five emotions work together. They are Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear and Disgust. Each one is a small, colourful character. Joy is the leader, and she wants Riley to be happy all the time. She thinks Sadness is useless. But one day Joy and Sadness get lost far away from the control centre, and Riley's feelings start to go wrong.

The film is funny, but it is also clever. It explains that sadness is not a bad thing. Sometimes we need it to understand ourselves and other people.

The sequel, Inside Out 2, came out in 2024. It added new emotions, for example Anxiety.

questions.q: Where does most of the story happen?
Who is the leader of the emotions at first?
What does the film say about sadness?
o: It is not a bad thing

title: A Rat Who Can Cook
ru: Мультфильм Pixar о крысе Реми, который мечтает стать поваром в Париже.
text:
Ratatouille is a Pixar film from 2007. Brad Bird directed it. It is about Remy, a rat with a very unusual dream. He wants to be a chef!

Remy has a much better nose than other rats. He does not want to eat rubbish. He wants to cook real food with good ingredients. His family thinks this is a silly idea, because people hate rats, especially in kitchens.

One day Remy gets lost and arrives in Paris. He finds a famous restaurant and meets Linguini, a young man who works there. Linguini cannot cook at all, but Remy can. So they find a funny way to work together. Remy hides under Linguini's chef's hat and pulls his hair to control his hands.

The film shows Paris in a beautiful way, and the food looks delicious. Later, a strict food critic called Anton Ego comes to the restaurant, and everything depends on one dinner.

The message is simple and nice: a great cook can come from anywhere.

questions.q: What is Remy's dream?
Where does Remy hide?
Who is Anton Ego?

title: A Viking and His Dragon
ru: Мультфильм DreamWorks о юном викинге Иккинге, который подружился с драконом.
text:
How to Train Your Dragon is a DreamWorks film from 2010. It is based on children's books by the British writer Cressida Cowell.

The story happens on Berk, a cold island where Vikings live. The Vikings and the dragons are enemies. The dragons steal sheep, and the Vikings fight them. For a young Viking, killing a dragon is the most important thing.

The hero is Hiccup, the son of the chief. He is thin, clumsy and not very strong, so the other Vikings laugh at him. But he is smart and good at making machines. One night he catches a rare black dragon. He wants to kill it, but when he looks into its eyes, he can't do it. He gives the dragon a name, Toothless, and slowly they become best friends.

The flying scenes are some of the best in any animated film, and the music is wonderful. The film was so popular that it got two sequels, TV series and, in 2025, a live-action remake.

questions.q: Where do the Vikings live?
o: On a cold island called Berk

questions.q: What is Hiccup good at?
What is the dragon's name?

title: Many Spider-People
ru: Мультфильм о подростке Майлзе Моралесе, который становится Человеком-пауком.
text:
Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse came out in 2018. Sony made it, and it won the Oscar for the best animated film.

The hero is not Peter Parker. He is Miles Morales, a teenager from Brooklyn, New York. Miles is a normal boy. He likes music and street art, and he is nervous at his new school. Then a special spider bites him, and he gets strange powers.

Soon Miles learns an amazing secret. There are many different worlds, and each world has its own Spider-Man. Because of a dangerous machine, several Spider-People come to his world. There is an older, tired Peter Parker, a cool Spider-Woman called Gwen, and even a funny spider-pig! They must help Miles and then go back home.

The film looks different from all other animated films. It is like a comic book that moves, with bright colours, lines and words on the screen. Many people think it is the best Spider-Man film ever. The sequel, Across the Spider-Verse, came out in 2023.

questions.q: Where is Miles from?
What is special about the film's style?
o: It looks like a moving comic book

questions.q: Why do other Spider-People come to Miles's world?
o: Because they are lost on holiday

title: The Boy Who Controls the Air
ru: Мультсериал о мальчике Аанге, который должен вернуть мир четырём народам.
text:
Avatar: The Last Airbender is an American animated series. It was on Nickelodeon from 2005 to 2008. The creators were Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko.

In this world there are four nations: Water, Earth, Fire and Air. Some people can control one element. This skill is called bending. Only one person, the Avatar, can control all four elements and keep peace in the world.

At the start of the show, the Fire Nation is at war with everyone. Two teenagers from the Water Tribe, Katara and her brother Sokka, find a boy in the ice. His name is Aang. He is twelve years old, and he is the new Avatar. He is also the last airbender. Now he must learn water, earth and fire before it is too late.

The show has three seasons, and each season is called a "Book". It looks like a cartoon for kids, but the story is deep and the characters change a lot. Many fans think Zuko, an angry prince, has the best story of all.

questions.q: How many nations are there?
Where do Katara and Sokka find Aang?

title: Speedrunning: Finishing Games Very, Very Fast
ru: Что такое спидраны и почему люди проходят игры за минуты
text:
Most people play a game slowly. They explore, read the story and enjoy the music. Speedrunners do the opposite: they try to finish a game as fast as possible. A game that normally takes twenty hours can sometimes be completed in less than one hour.

How is this possible? First, speedrunners know every part of the game perfectly. They have played the same levels hundreds or even thousands of times. They know the shortest routes and the exact moment to jump or attack. Second, they often use glitches. A glitch is a mistake in the game's code. For example, a player might go through a wall or skip a whole part of the level. Some glitches are so difficult that it takes months of practice to do them correctly.

Speedruns are divided into categories. In an "any%" run, you can use any method to reach the end, including glitches. In a "100%" run, you have to collect everything. Some categories don't allow glitches at all. The times are recorded on websites like speedrun.com, where runners compare their results.

Speedrunning has also become a popular thing to watch. Games Done Quick is a series of charity marathons in the USA, where runners play live for a whole week. Viewers donate money, and the events have raised a lot of money for charity over the years.

Although it looks crazy, speedrunning is similar to a sport. It needs patience, practice and a strong memory. And if a runner fails at the last second, the audience feels the pain too. Have you ever tried to beat your own record?

Hollow Knight came out in 2017. It was created by Team Cherry, a very small studio from Australia. The game is completely different from Stardew Valley. You play as a small, silent knight who explores Hallownest, a dark underground kingdom of insects that has fallen into ruin. The world is beautiful and mysterious, but the game is hard. You will die many times, and you will have to learn every enemy's movements. Fans waited years for the sequel, Hollow Knight: Silksong, which finally came out in 2025.

Although these two games are very different, they have something in common. Both were made with a lot of love and attention to detail. They show that you don't need a huge team to create a world that millions of people want to live in.

On paper, Succession sounds like the least relatable show imaginable. The secret lies in the characters. Logan, played with terrifying intensity by Brian Cox, treats his children less like family and more like employees who must constantly prove their loyalty. Kendall desperately wants to be the heir but keeps tripping over his own insecurities. title: Why Sitcoms Still Work

ru: Почему ситкомы до сих пор популярны, хотя формату больше полувека

Every few years, critics announce that the sitcom is dead. Prestige dramas get the awards, streaming services chase the next big fantasy epic, and short videos compete for every spare minute of our attention. And yet, when people come home exhausted after a long day, a surprising number of them reach for the same thing: a twenty-minute comedy they have already seen a dozen times.

Part of the reason is structure. A classic sitcom is built around a fixed place and a small group of people who cannot easily escape each other. Friends had its apartment and its coffee shop, The Office had a dull paper company in Pennsylvania, and Brooklyn Nine-Nine had a police station full of lovable oddballs. The setting barely changes, so the comedy has to come from the characters themselves. Once you know how each person reacts, half the fun is predicting the disaster before it happens.

That predictability, which sounds like a weakness, is actually the secret ingredient. Psychologists often point out that familiar stories are comforting because they demand very little from us. We know nobody will die in a shocking twist, and we know that whatever goes wrong will more or less be fixed by the end of the episode. In an uncertain world, that is a small but genuine relief.

Sitcoms have also proved remarkably good at adapting. The older multi-camera shows were filmed in front of a live audience, with laughter clearly audible after every joke. Later, single-camera comedies such as The Office dropped the laugh track altogether and borrowed the style of a documentary, with characters glancing awkwardly at the camera. The format changed its clothes, but not its heart.

Finally, sitcoms grow old with their viewers in an unusual way. Because a series might run for seven or ten seasons, fans spend years with the same group of people. The characters start to feel less like fictional creations and more like distant friends, which explains why reunions and rewatch podcasts are so popular.

So the sitcom is not dead; it has simply stopped trying to be fashionable. As long as people need somewhere cosy to rest their brains, there will be a sofa, a group of friends and a problem that gets solved just before the credits roll.

ru: Как стриминговые сервисы воюют за зрителя и что это значит для нас
text:
Not so long ago, watching TV online felt like a clever shortcut. You paid one company a modest monthly fee and got access to an enormous library of films and series. That company was usually Netflix, which had started out in the late 1990s by posting DVDs to customers and switched to streaming in 2007. For a few years, it had the field almost entirely to itself.

Then the big studios realised they were handing their most valuable shows to a competitor. One by one, they pulled their content back and launched platforms of their own. Disney+ arrived in 2019, bringing Marvel, Star Wars and Pixar under one roof. Warner Bros. launched HBO Max, later renamed simply Max. Apple, Amazon and several others joined the race. Journalists began calling this period the streaming wars, and the name stuck.

For viewers, the early stage of the war was rather pleasant. Companies spent huge sums on original series in order to attract subscribers, and the result was a golden age of choice. Big-budget fantasy, ambitious sci-fi and quirky small comedies all found a home. If you enjoyed television, there had never been a better time to be alive.

However, wars are expensive, and eventually someone has to pay. Over the past few years, prices have crept up, cheaper plans with adverts have appeared, and Netflix began cracking down on people sharing passwords outside their household. Many series that were not immediately popular have been cancelled after one or two seasons, sometimes on a cliffhanger, which leaves loyal fans feeling betrayed.

There is also the problem of fragmentation. To watch everything people are talking about, you might need four or five subscriptions, and the total bill can end up higher than old-fashioned cable ever was. Ironically, some services are now bundling together, which looks suspiciously like the cable packages streaming was supposed to replace.

So who is winning? Honestly, it is too early to say, and the answer may be nobody. What seems clear is that the era of one cheap subscription for everything is over. The smartest viewers now treat streaming like a gym membership: sign up for a month, watch the series you care about, cancel, and move on to the next platform.

title: How an Animated Film Is Made
about: The making of a computer-animated feature
ru: Этапы создания полнометражного анимационного фильма — от идеи до рендеринга
text:
When we watch a ninety-minute animated film, it is easy to forget that every single frame had to be deliberately created. Nothing is captured by accident, the way a live-action camera might catch a bird flying past. That is why a big computer-animated feature usually takes several years and hundreds of artists to complete.

It all begins with a story, and the story changes constantly. Writers produce a script, but before anything expensive is made, story artists turn it into storyboards: rough sketches that show each shot, a bit like a comic book. These drawings are then edited together with temporary voices and music into something called an animatic. Watching this crude version, the team can tell whether a joke lands or a scene drags. Studios are famous for throwing away huge chunks of a film at this stage and starting again.

Next come the voices. In most American studios, actors record their lines before the animation is done, so animators can match the movement of the characters to the performance. Actors often record alone in a booth, reacting to partners who are not actually there, which is harder than it sounds.

Meanwhile, the world of the film is being designed. Artists create characters, costumes and locations on paper, and modellers then build them as 3D objects in the computer. Each character is given a rig, a kind of invisible skeleton with hundreds of controls, so it can bend, blink and smile.

Only then does the animation itself begin. Animators work shot by shot, posing characters frame by frame to create believable movement. A good animator is really an actor who performs through a mouse and keyboard, and a few seconds of footage can take a week of work.

Finally, lighting artists add mood and atmosphere, effects specialists create water, fire and hair, and powerful computers render every frame into a finished image. This stage alone can take enormous amounts of processing time.

Toy Story, released by Pixar in 1995, was the first feature film made entirely on computers, and the technology has advanced dramatically since then. Yet the basic lesson has not changed: software can make images beautiful, but only a strong story, rewritten again and again, makes an audience care.

title: Dubbing vs Subtitles
about: Dubbing, subtitles and voice-over around the world
ru: Дубляж или субтитры: что выбирают разные страны и почему спор не утихает
text:
Few questions divide film lovers quite as sharply as this one: should you watch a foreign film dubbed into your own language, or in the original with subtitles? Both sides tend to hold their opinions with almost religious passion, and both have a point.

Interestingly, the answer often depends on where you grew up. Countries such as Germany, Italy, Spain and France have a long tradition of dubbing, and their voice actors are highly respected professionals. In fact, some famous Hollywood stars have had the same local voice for decades, and audiences would be shocked to hear anyone else. By contrast, the Netherlands and the Scandinavian countries mostly subtitle foreign content, particularly for adults. Russia is a special case, since single-voice or multi-voice voice-over, where the original is still faintly audible underneath, has long been a familiar compromise.

Fans of subtitles argue that the actor's voice is part of the performance. Tone, accent and timing are carefully chosen, and replacing them changes the character. There is also the practical bonus that you hear the real language, which is why people in subtitling countries are often said to be better at English, although other factors certainly play a role as well.

Defenders of dubbing have strong arguments too. Reading subtitles means your eyes are constantly jumping to the bottom of the screen, so you may miss facial expressions or details in the background. For children, older viewers or anyone who is tired, a dubbed version is simply more relaxing. A skilful dub can also adapt jokes and wordplay that would fall flat if translated literally.

Of course, bad examples exist on both sides. Everyone has seen a dub where the lips move long after the words have stopped, or subtitles that summarise a two-minute argument in five words. Translation is always a matter of compromise, and neither method is perfect.

Streaming has made the debate more personal. Today, you can usually choose the audio track and subtitle language with a couple of clicks, so each viewer can decide for themselves. For learners of English, there is an obvious recommendation: try the original sound with English subtitles. It is tiring at first, but your ears will gradually adjust, and you will hear the story the way it was meant to be heard.

title: Learning English with TV Shows
about: Using series to improve your English
ru: Как с пользой учить английский по сериалам — практические советы
text:
Almost everyone who has learned English to a high level has a similar story: at some point, they got hooked on a series and started watching it in the original. It is an appealing idea, because it turns study into entertainment. But simply leaving the TV on in English will not magically make you fluent. To get real value from it, you need a bit of strategy.

First, choose the right show. Beginners often jump straight into complex dramas full of legal jargon or medieval politics, then give up after ten minutes. It is much wiser to start with something built on everyday conversation, such as a sitcom or a family drama. Episodes are short, the situations are familiar, and the same phrases come up again and again. Animated series can also work well, because voice actors tend to speak clearly.

Second, think carefully about subtitles. Subtitles in your own language are fine for relaxing, but they do very little for your English, since your brain simply reads the translation. English subtitles are far more useful: you hear the words and see them at the same time, which helps you connect sounds to spelling. Once you feel comfortable, try switching subtitles off for scenes you have already watched.

Third, be active rather than passive. Pick one short scene, maybe two or three minutes long, and watch it several times. The first time, just follow the story. Then pause and note down any expressions you did not know, look them up, and add the most useful ones to a flashcard app. Finally, watch the scene again and try repeating the lines out loud along with the actors. This technique, known as shadowing, does wonders for your pronunciation and rhythm.

Fourth, do not panic about accents. British, American, Australian and Irish shows all sound different, and it is perfectly normal to find some of them harder at first. Stick with one variety for a while, then branch out.

Most importantly, watch something you genuinely enjoy. Motivation is the fuel of language learning, and a series you love will keep you coming back far more reliably than any textbook. If you find yourself thinking about the characters after you switch off the screen, you are already on the right track.

title: Storytelling in Video Games
about: Narrative in games: The Last of Us, Mass Effect, Disco Elysium
ru: Чем рассказ истории в играх отличается от кино и книг
text:
For a long time, stories in video games were treated as decoration. A princess needed rescuing, an alien army needed defeating, and a few lines of text explained why. Nobody expected much more, because the real point was the gameplay. Today, however, many players choose a game precisely because of its story, and some games are discussed with the same seriousness as novels or films.

What makes game storytelling unique is that the audience takes part. In a film, you watch a character make a difficult decision; in a game, you often make it yourself. Series such as Mass Effect, created by BioWare, allowed players to shape relationships and political outcomes over three whole games, so two friends could end up with surprisingly different stories. Disco Elysium, released in 2019, went even further, turning almost the entire experience into conversations, choices and the inner voices of a troubled detective.

Other games tell a fixed story but use interactivity to make it hit harder. The Last of Us, released by Naughty Dog in 2013, follows a hardened smuggler and a teenage girl travelling across a ruined America. The plot itself is linear, yet because the player spends hours protecting the girl, the bond between the characters feels earned rather than simply shown. It is one thing to watch someone care for another person; it is quite another to do it yourself.

Games also have a quieter technique, often called environmental storytelling. Instead of explaining everything through cutscenes, designers leave clues in the world: a half-written note, a child's drawing on a wall, an abandoned room with the table still set for dinner. Curious players piece together what happened, and the story they discover feels more personal because they found it themselves.

Of course, there are tensions. A game might present its hero as kind and thoughtful in cutscenes, then ask the player to defeat hundreds of enemies without a second thought. Critics even invented a clumsy term for this mismatch between story and gameplay. The best studios work hard to make the two support each other.

Whether games are art is a debate that now feels slightly outdated. The more interesting question is what stories only games can tell, and designers are still discovering the answer.

title: Fandoms and Fan Theories
about: Fan communities, fan theories and fan fiction
ru: Как устроены фанатские сообщества и почему люди так любят теории
text:
Being a fan used to be a fairly private hobby. You watched your favourite show, maybe collected a few magazines, and discussed it with the one friend who shared your enthusiasm. The internet changed all that. Today, almost every popular series, film franchise or game has a fandom: a community of people who analyse it, celebrate it and sometimes argue about it with astonishing intensity.

Fandoms are not new, of course. Star Trek fans in the 1960s and 70s organised conventions, wrote stories about their favourite characters and even campaigned to save the show when it was in danger. What the internet added was speed and scale. A clue hidden in the background of a new episode can be spotted, screenshotted and debated by millions of people within hours.

One of the most enjoyable fandom activities is building fan theories. These are attempts to explain mysteries the creators have not revealed yet, or to find hidden connections between stories. Shows with complex mythology, such as Lost in the 2000s or Game of Thrones in the 2010s, generated thousands of theories, from the brilliant to the completely ridiculous. Occasionally, fans guess correctly years in advance, which is both thrilling for them and a headache for the writers.

Why do people put so much energy into this? Partly because it extends the pleasure of the story. A good theory lets you stay inside a fictional world long after the episode has ended. It is also a social activity: sharing a clever idea and seeing others react to it creates a real sense of belonging. And for many fans, creative projects like fan art and fan fiction are a way to develop their own skills as artists and writers.

Naturally, fandoms have a darker side. Some fans feel such ownership of a story that they react angrily when it goes in a direction they dislike, and actors have been harassed online simply for playing an unpopular character. Healthy fandom means remembering that the story belongs, first of all, to the people who create it.

Still, at their best, fan communities are among the most creative and welcoming corners of the internet. If you are learning English, joining one is also an excellent way to read and write every day about something you genuinely love.

title: Spoilers and Why We Hate Them
ru: Почему спойлеры так раздражают и действительно ли они портят удовольствие
text:
There are few modern crimes as widely condemned as the spoiler. Reveal the ending of a new series to a friend who has not finished it, and you may find yourself treated as if you had stolen their wallet. Social media only makes things worse: after a major episode airs, fans mute keywords, avoid entire websites and sometimes leave group chats until they have caught up.

But why do we care so much? After all, most of us happily rewatch favourite films whose endings we know by heart. The answer seems to be that a spoiler takes away a particular kind of pleasure, the experience of discovering something for the first time. When a story is carefully built towards a surprise, being told the surprise in advance can feel like someone opening your birthday present before you arrive.

Interestingly, research suggests the situation is more complicated. In a well-known study from the University of California, San Diego, published in 2011, participants read short stories, some of them with the ending revealed beforehand. Many readers actually enjoyed the spoiled versions slightly more. One explanation is that knowing where a story is going frees your attention to notice style, character and clever details you might otherwise miss.

That does not mean spoilers are harmless. The study used short fiction, not a series you have followed for years, and the emotional investment is quite different. What is more, part of the fun of modern television is watching together, at the same moment, and reacting as a community. Having the big twist ruined removes you from that shared experience.

Spoiler culture has also created its own etiquette. Most people agree that you should add a clear warning before discussing major plot points, especially for recent releases. How long a story stays spoiler-protected is a matter of heated debate. A week? A year? Forever? Nobody really agrees, although almost everyone accepts that classic films from decades ago are fair game.

Perhaps the healthiest attitude lies somewhere in the middle. Good stories survive spoilers, because they are about more than a single twist. Still, if you know someone is halfway through a series they adore, the kind thing is simply to keep quiet. A little patience costs nothing, and your friendship may depend on it.

title: The Age of Binge-Watching
about: Binge-watching and how streaming changed our habits
ru: Как запойный просмотр сериалов изменил и зрителей, и сами сериалы
text:
It starts innocently enough. You decide to watch one episode before bed. The credits roll, a countdown appears in the corner, and before you have time to think, the next episode has started. Three hours later, you are still on the sofa, promising yourself that this really is the last one. Welcome to binge-watching, one of the defining habits of the streaming age.

Of course, people watched several episodes in a row long before streaming, thanks to DVD box sets. But the habit went mainstream when Netflix started releasing entire seasons of its original series on a single day in the early 2010s. Suddenly, there was no need to wait a week for the next instalment. The word became so common that the British dictionary Collins chose binge-watch as its word of the year in 2015.

The change affected how stories are written. When a show is released weekly, each episode needs to work on its own and leave viewers eager to return. When it is designed to be watched in one go, writers can treat a whole season more like a very long film, with slower build-ups and fewer reminders of what happened earlier. Many streaming series are, in effect, ten-hour movies chopped into pieces.

Binge-watching has clear advantages. It lets you immerse yourself completely in a fictional world and follow complex plots without forgetting important details. For busy people, a free weekend spent with a great series can be a genuine pleasure.

Yet there are downsides. Staying up late to finish a season is hardly good for sleep, and critics argue that stories consumed so quickly are also forgotten quickly. With weekly shows, fans spend days discussing theories and anticipating what comes next; with a binge, the whole thing can be over before the conversation even starts. Some viewers also notice a strange emptiness when they reach the final episode, as if a holiday had ended too soon.

Interestingly, several streaming services have recently gone back to releasing episodes weekly, at least for their biggest shows, hoping to keep people talking for longer. Perhaps the ideal lies in a balance: binge when a story truly grips you, but occasionally let yourself wait. Anticipation, after all, is part of the pleasure.

title: The Rise of Anime in the West
about: Anime outside Japan: from Astro Boy to Demon Slayer
ru: Как японская анимация прошла путь от нишевого хобби до мейнстрима на Западе
text:
Not long ago, admitting that you watched anime in Europe or North America could earn you a few strange looks. It was seen as a niche interest for teenagers and dedicated collectors who traded tapes and read fan-made translations. Today, anime series top streaming charts, anime films fill cinemas, and major Hollywood studios compete to produce live-action adaptations. How did this happen?

The story actually begins in the 1960s, when Astro Boy, created by the legendary artist Osamu Tezuka, was broadcast on American television. However, for decades most Western viewers had no idea that many of the cartoons they watched came from Japan, because the shows were heavily edited and their origins were rarely mentioned.

The real breakthrough came in the late 1990s. Pokémon became a worldwide phenomenon, and a generation of children grew up with its games, cards and animated series. At around the same time, Cartoon Network in the United States began showing action series such as Dragon Ball Z in its Toonami block, introducing young viewers to longer storylines and more dramatic battles than typical Western cartoons offered.

Critical respect followed. Spirited Away, directed by Hayao Miyazaki at Studio Ghibli, won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2003, proving that Japanese animation could be regarded as serious art. Many adults who had dismissed anime as children's entertainment suddenly began to reconsider.

The internet and streaming did the rest. Services such as Crunchyroll started offering new episodes with subtitles soon after they aired in Japan, so Western fans no longer had to wait months or years. Later, the big streaming platforms began investing in anime themselves. Series like Attack on Titan and Demon Slayer became global talking points, and their fans organised watch parties across time zones.

Why does anime resonate so strongly? One reason is its remarkable range. There are anime about sport, cooking, office life, ancient history, romance and space opera, aimed at every age group. Another is its willingness to treat emotions seriously, allowing characters to grieve, fail and grow over long story arcs.

Of course, some viewers still find certain conventions odd, from dramatic facial expressions to very long fight scenes. But anime no longer needs anyone's approval. It has become a genuinely global art form.

title: The Voices Behind the Cartoons
about: Voice actors: Mel Blanc, Dan Castellaneta, Tom Kenny
ru: Кто такие актёры озвучивания и почему их работа сложнее, чем кажется
text:
Think of your favourite cartoon character and you will probably hear their voice in your head immediately. Yet most people have no idea what the person behind that voice looks like. Voice actors are some of the most recognisable performers in the world, and at the same time some of the most invisible.

The art has a long history. In the golden age of American animation, Mel Blanc became famous as the man of a thousand voices, performing Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and many other Looney Tunes characters. For many years, audiences heard him in almost every short the studio released, often playing several characters in the same scene. Blanc showed that a single talented performer could give life to an entire cast.

Modern television animation has its own legends. Dan Castellaneta has voiced Homer Simpson since the character first appeared in the late 1980s, alongside many other residents of Springfield. Tom Kenny is the voice of SpongeBob SquarePants, and his cheerful, high-pitched performance is a huge part of the character's charm. Viewers who hear these actors speaking normally in interviews are often amazed at how different they sound.

So what makes the job so demanding? For one thing, voice actors have to express everything with sound alone: a smile, a shrug, a moment of fear. They frequently record in a small booth, often alone, imagining the other characters and the action around them. A single session can involve shouting, crying and laughing for hours, which is exhausting for the throat. Many performers also juggle several characters in one show, switching between them within seconds.

In recent decades, big animated films have increasingly cast famous Hollywood stars. Robin Williams, for example, brought astonishing improvisational energy to the Genie in Disney's Aladdin in 1992, and his performance changed how studios thought about casting. The trend has its critics, who point out that experienced voice specialists sometimes lose roles to celebrities chosen mainly for publicity.

Whatever the case, the best voice performances are those we stop noticing. When a character on screen simply feels alive, it is because someone in a dark booth, far from the cameras, poured their whole personality into a microphone. Next time the credits roll, it is worth taking a moment to read their names.

title: Why Villains Steal the Show
about: Villains in film: Scar, Hans Gruber, the Joker, Loki
ru: Почему злодеи часто интереснее героев и чем запоминаются лучшие из них
text:
Ask a group of friends to name their favourite film character and a surprising number will choose the bad guy. Audiences may cheer when the hero wins, but it is often the villain they quote, imitate and remember for years. Why do the characters we are supposed to dislike so often steal the show?

One reason is freedom. Heroes usually have to follow certain rules: they must be brave, fair and likeable, at least by the end. Villains have no such restrictions. They can be witty, cruel, elegant or completely unpredictable, and actors clearly relish the chance to play them. Alan Rickman as the calm, sarcastic thief Hans Gruber in Die Hard is a classic example. He turned what could have been a standard action-movie bad guy into someone genuinely fascinating to watch.

Another reason is motivation. The hero's goal is often simple: save the city, protect the family, stop the bad guy. The villain, on the other hand, is the one who sets the story in motion, so writers tend to give them the more interesting desires. Scar in Disney's The Lion King, released in 1994, is driven by jealousy and wounded pride, emotions that almost everyone has felt at some point, even if we would never act on them the way he does.

The best modern villains blur the line between good and evil. Heath Ledger's Joker in The Dark Knight, from 2008, is terrifying precisely because he seems to have no clear motive at all, and he challenges the hero's beliefs more than his fists. Loki in the Marvel films became so popular that he eventually received his own series, where his tricks were balanced by moments of loneliness and doubt. Audiences love a villain who might, just possibly, be redeemed.

There is also a psychological explanation. Watching a villain allows us to explore dark feelings from a safe distance. We can enjoy their confidence and rule-breaking without facing any real consequences. When the story ends, we return to our ordinary lives, perhaps a little relieved that we are not like them.

Finally, a great villain makes the hero better. A victory only matters if the opponent is truly dangerous. So perhaps we should not feel guilty for loving the bad guys. Without them, our heroes would have nothing to prove.

title: Counter-Strike: From a Mod to a Legend
ru: Counter-Strike — как фанатский мод стал одним из главных шутеров в мире
text:
Few games have lasted as long as Counter-Strike. It started in 1999, not as a real product, but as a mod: a free fan-made version of another game, Half-Life. Two young developers, Minh Le and Jess Cliffe, created it. It became so popular that Valve, the company behind Half-Life, hired them and bought the game.

The idea has hardly changed since then. Two teams of five players fight on a small map. One team, the terrorists, tries to plant a bomb. The other team, the counter-terrorists, tries to stop them or defuse the bomb. If you die in a round, you don't come back until the next round. Because of this, every mistake matters, and players are careful and slow rather than wild.

There is also an economy. After each round, you get money, and you use it to buy weapons and armour. If your team loses several rounds, you may need to save money instead of buying the best equipment. So Counter-Strike is not only about fast reactions but also about planning and teamwork.

Over the years, Valve has released several versions. Counter-Strike: Global Offensive came out in 2012 and was played for more than ten years. In 2023, it was replaced by Counter-Strike 2, which runs on a newer engine.

Counter-Strike has also been one of the biggest esports for a long time. The most important tournaments are called Majors, and teams from Europe, the CIS, Brazil and many other regions have won them.

title: Civilization: History in Your Hands
ru: Civilization — пошаговая стратегия, где ведёшь народ от каменного века к космосу
text:
Imagine starting with one small group of people in the Stone Age and leading them all the way to a spaceship. That is the idea of Civilization, one of the most famous strategy games of all time. The American designer Sid Meier created the first game in 1991, and the series has continued ever since. Civilization VI came out in 2016, and Civilization VII in 2025.

Civilization is a turn-based game. This means that you and the other players take turns, like in chess. Nobody is in a hurry, so you have time to think. You build cities, grow food, research new technologies and meet other nations. At first, you are learning how to make pottery or ride horses. Several thousand years later, you are building airports and computers.

You can play as many real nations and their famous leaders, for example Rome, Egypt, China or Russia. However, the history you create is your own. In your game, the Aztecs might invent electricity before England does.

There are different ways to win. You can conquer everyone, although war is often slow and expensive. You can also win through science by sending people to space, or through culture, if the whole world loves your music, art and tourism.

Civilization has a dangerous reputation. Many players say they sat down for a short game in the evening and suddenly noticed that the sun was rising. There is always one more city to build and one more technology to research. If you have never played it, choose a free weekend to start.

title: Resident Evil: The Mansion Where Horror Began
ru: Resident Evil — серия, которая сделала «survival horror» популярным жанром
text:
In 1996, the Japanese company Capcom released a game for the first PlayStation. In Japan it was called Biohazard, but in the West it got the name Resident Evil. It helped to make a whole genre popular: survival horror.

The story begins near a quiet American city called Raccoon City. A team of special police officers goes into the forest to find their missing colleagues. Chased by strange creatures, they run into an old mansion. You play as Chris Redfield or Jill Valentine, and you soon discover that the house is full of dangerous secrets, locked doors and puzzles.

What made the game so scary was not blood but the feeling of weakness. You have very few bullets and not much medicine, so you often need to decide whether to fight or run away. Even saving the game is limited. You need a special item and a typewriter to do it. The camera also stays in fixed positions, so you often hear something before you can see it.

Since then, the series has changed many times. Resident Evil 4 in 2005 added much more action. Resident Evil 7 in 2017 moved the camera to first person and became frightening again. Capcom has also remade several older parts with modern graphics, for example Resident Evil 2 in 2019 and Resident Evil 4 in 2023.

There have been films and series based on the games, although most fans agree the games are much better. If you like horror but hate cheap jump scares, the classic Resident Evil games are worth trying. Just play them with the lights on.

title: Undertale: Mercy Instead of Fighting
ru: Undertale — инди-RPG одного автора, где врагов можно пощадить
text:
In most role-playing games, you get stronger by defeating enemies. Undertale, released in 2015, asks a simple question: what if you didn't have to hurt anyone at all?

The game was made almost entirely by one person, the American developer Toby Fox. He wrote the story, designed the game and even composed all the music. He had only a small budget, which he had raised from fans on Kickstarter. The graphics look very simple, like an old game from the early 1990s. However, that didn't stop Undertale from becoming one of the most loved indie games ever.

You play as a human child who falls into the Underground, a world where monsters have lived for a long time. Many of them are not evil at all. There is Toriel, a kind, motherly goat-like monster, and two skeleton brothers, Sans and Papyrus, who are among the funniest characters in games.

The battles are unusual. When an enemy attacks, you control a small red heart and dodge bullets, a bit like in an arcade shooter. But you can also talk to monsters, tell jokes, give them compliments and finally spare them. Every enemy, even the bosses, can be defeated without violence.

The most interesting part is that the game remembers your choices, sometimes even after you restart it. If you are cruel, the world and its characters react to it. That is why many players have finished the game two or three times, in different ways.

If you have played it, you probably still remember the music. If you haven't, try to avoid spoilers, because the surprises are a big part of the fun. After Undertale, Toby Fox started a new project, Deltarune.

title: Is Esports a Real Sport?
about: Esports (about games): League of Legends, Counter-Strike and others

text:
Twenty-five years ago, playing video games for money sounded like a joke. Today, professional gamers play in front of full stadiums, and millions of people watch them online. This is esports, and it has become a huge industry.

The most popular esports are team games such as League of Legends, Counter-Strike and Dota 2, but there are also tournaments for fighting games, racing games, football games and even Tetris. The biggest event in League of Legends, the World Championship, has been held in stadiums in Asia, Europe and North America. One of its most famous players is Faker, from South Korea, who has won the title several times and is treated like a sports star at home.

Professional players usually belong to teams, just like football players. They have coaches and analysts, and they often live and train together. Many of them practise for ten or more hours a day. Careers are short. Most players retire before they are thirty, because younger players often have faster reactions.

So, is it a real sport? People who say no point out that players don't run or lift anything. People who say yes argue that chess is also called a sport, and that esports demands speed, strategy, teamwork and strong nerves under pressure. Esports has already been included as a medal event at the Asian Games, which is a strong argument for the second side.

Whatever you think, esports is a good way to learn English. Most international tournaments are broadcast in English, and commentators speak fast and clearly. If you watch a match of a game you know well, you'll understand much more than you expect.

title: Can Video Games Teach You English?
ru: Про игры: как с помощью видеоигр учить английский и что для этого лучше подходит
text:
Many people who speak English well will tell you the same thing: they learned a lot of it from video games, long before they studied it seriously. This isn't surprising. When you want to understand what a character is saying or how to finish a quest, you are much more motivated than when you read a textbook.

However, not all games are equally useful. In a racing game or a simple shooter, you mostly hear short commands and read menus. That's fine for a beginner, but you'll quickly stop learning new words. Story-driven games are much better. Role-playing games and adventure games are full of dialogue, letters, books and descriptions. Detective games are especially good, because you have to understand details to solve the case.

Here are a few tips. First, switch the language of the game to English, both the voices and the subtitles. Reading and listening at the same time helps you connect how a word looks with how it sounds. Second, choose a game you have already played in Russian. Since you know the story, you can guess new words from the context. Third, don't stop to translate every word. Look up only the words that appear again and again, and write them down or put them into flashcards.

Online games give you something that textbooks can't: real communication. If you play co-op games with people from other countries, you have to talk to them in English, quickly and without preparation. It can feel scary at first, but most players care about the game, not about your grammar.

Of course, games won't replace real practice. But if you have already spent hundreds of hours playing, why not make some of those hours useful?

title: How Game Music Is Made
about: Video game soundtracks (about games): Koji Kondo, Nobuo Uematsu, C418, Mick Gordon
ru: Про игры: как пишут музыку для игр — от 8-битных мелодий до адаптивных саундтреков
text:
Try to remember the music from a game you loved as a child. Chances are you can hum it right now, even if you haven't heard it for years. That is no accident. Game music is written under unusual conditions, and those conditions have shaped a surprisingly rich art form.

In the 1980s, composers worked with almost nothing. The Nintendo Entertainment System could play only a handful of sounds at the same time, so every note had to count. Koji Kondo, who wrote the music for Super Mario Bros. and The Legend of Zelda, had to create melodies that were catchy, fit into a tiny amount of memory and didn't become annoying after hundreds of loops. The fact that people still play his themes on pianos and in orchestras says a lot about how well he solved that puzzle. Similarly, Nobuo Uematsu's work on the Final Fantasy series showed that game music could be emotional and ambitious, not just background noise.

As technology improved, the limits disappeared, but a different challenge remained. Unlike a film, a game doesn't know what will happen next. A player might spend thirty seconds in a room or thirty minutes. That is why modern composers often write adaptive music: the soundtrack is split into layers that can be added or removed depending on the situation. When you are exploring, you might hear only strings; when an enemy appears, drums and brass join in, without any obvious cut.

There is no single style any more. The calm piano pieces that C418 (Daniel Rosenfeld) wrote for Minecraft are almost the opposite of the aggressive metal that Mick Gordon produced for Doom in 2016. Some soundtracks are recorded with full orchestras, while others are composed by one person on a laptop, as Toby Fox did for Undertale.

Game music has also left the screen. Concerts dedicated entirely to video game soundtracks now fill large halls around the world, and many listeners use these tracks to study or work, because the music was designed to support concentration without demanding attention. If you've never listened to a soundtrack on its own, give it a try. You might be surprised how much you notice when there is no gameplay to distract you.

title: Last One Standing: The Rise of Battle Royale
about: The battle royale genre (about games): DayZ mods, PUBG, Fortnite, Apex Legends, Warzone
ru: Про игры: откуда взялся жанр королевской битвы и почему он захватил мир
text:
Some genres develop slowly over decades. Battle royale, by contrast, went from an obscure mod to the most talked-about format in gaming almost overnight. Its story says a lot about how the modern games industry works.

The name comes from Battle Royale, a Japanese film from 2000 in which students are forced to compete on an island until only one survives. The concept of being dropped into a closed area with dozens of opponents and whatever you can find on the ground was obviously attractive to game designers, but for a long time nobody built a hit around it.

That changed thanks to Brendan Greene, an Irish designer better known by his online name, PlayerUnknown. In the early 2010s, he made battle royale mods for the military shooters Arma 2 and Arma 3. They were rough around the edges, but they established the rules that almost every later game follows: everyone starts with nothing, weapons are scattered randomly, and the playable area keeps shrinking, forcing survivors to meet.

In 2017, Greene's ideas became a full game, PlayerUnknown's Battlegrounds, usually shortened to PUBG. It sold millions of copies while still in early access. A few months later, Epic Games added a free battle royale mode to Fortnite, and it grew even faster, thanks to its cartoon style and building mechanics. Then Respawn released Apex Legends in 2019, adding heroes with special abilities, and in 2020 Call of Duty entered the race with Warzone.

Why did the genre catch on so quickly? Partly because every match tells a different story. You never know where you'll land, what you'll find or who you'll meet. Losing hurts, but a new match is only a minute away. The genre also happened to be perfect for streaming: viewers love the tension of the final few players, and the free-to-play model meant that anyone watching could join in the same evening.

Critics argue that the genre has become repetitive, and it is true that many copies disappeared as fast as they appeared. Still, the core idea has proved remarkably durable, and elements of it now appear in games that have nothing to do with shooting at all.

title: Outer Wilds: A Solar System in Twenty-Two Minutes
ru: Outer Wilds — космическая головоломка, где единственный прогресс — это знания
text:
Most games reward you with things: better weapons, more health, new abilities. Outer Wilds, released in 2019 by the small American studio Mobius Digital and published by Annapurna Interactive, gives you almost nothing of the kind. The only thing you collect is knowledge, and that turns out to be far more exciting than it sounds.

You play as a young astronaut from a tiny planet in a tiny solar system. On the day of your first flight, something goes badly wrong: after about twenty-two minutes, the sun explodes. Then you wake up again at the start of the same day, with the same twenty-two minutes ahead of you. Why this happens, and whether it can be stopped, is the mystery at the heart of the game. No big spoilers here, because discovering it yourself is the whole point.

The solar system is small, but every planet is a hand-crafted puzzle that changes over time. On one world, sand slowly flows from one planet to its twin, burying some places and revealing others. Another planet is gradually falling apart. Scattered across all of them are the ruins and writings of an ancient race called the Nomai, who were investigating the same mysteries long before you.

What makes Outer Wilds unusual is that nothing stops you from going anywhere from the very first loop. In theory, you could reach the ending in a few minutes, if only you knew what to do. Your ship keeps a log of clues, and progress happens entirely in your head. That is also why the game is so easy to spoil: a single hint can destroy an hour of discovery.

It isn't a game for everyone. The flying controls take time to master, and some players find the time pressure stressful rather than exciting. But for those who enjoy it, the moment when several clues suddenly connect is one of the most satisfying feelings in gaming. Many fans say they wish they could forget everything and play it again for the first time, which is probably the highest compliment a mystery can receive.

title: StarCraft: The Game That Built Esports in Korea
ru: StarCraft — стратегия в реальном времени, ставшая национальным спортом Южной Кореи
text:
When people talk about the birth of esports, one game comes up again and again: StarCraft. Released by the American company Blizzard Entertainment in 1998, it was a real-time strategy game set in a distant part of the galaxy. Nobody expected it to become something close to a national sport on the other side of the world.

The game features three very different races. The Terrans are humans with tanks, soldiers and buildings that can fly. The Zerg are an alien swarm that wins through numbers and speed. The Protoss are an advanced alien race with powerful but expensive units. What impressed players at the time was that the three sides felt completely different to play, and yet none of them was clearly stronger. Balancing such different factions is extremely hard, and StarCraft, especially after its expansion Brood War, got remarkably close to perfect.

The game's success in South Korea came from a combination of factors. The country was rapidly building fast internet connections, and computer clubs known as PC bangs were opening everywhere, giving young people a cheap place to play together. StarCraft became the game of choice in those clubs. Before long, there were professional leagues, sponsored teams and even TV channels broadcasting matches. Top players such as Lim Yo-hwan, known as BoxeR, became celebrities with huge fan clubs.

Watching a professional StarCraft match is a strange experience for beginners. Players control their armies and economies at the same time, and the best of them perform hundreds of actions per minute. A small mistake in the first few minutes can decide a game half an hour later. Commentators explain what is going on, but it still looks like organised chaos.

In 2010, Blizzard released StarCraft II, which took the series into a new era of online tournaments and streaming. The real-time strategy genre is less dominant today than it once was, having lost ground to team games like League of Legends and Dota 2, which, interestingly, grew out of fan-made maps for Blizzard's own strategy games. Still, many of the things we now take for granted in esports, from professional teams to live commentary, were first tried out with StarCraft.

title: The Witness Who Saw Too Much

text:
